source_access.scope: Complete selected abstract and publisher landing page read. The original supplemental spreadsheet request returned 403 and the full-text link redirected to the abstract; no target-table read is claimed. Independent COG5 membrane evidence supports retaining the broad location.

Protected abstract retained; the distinct genuine full variant is publicly available at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2173297/. Results on COG purification and Figure 1 identify two Cog5-containing fractions; whether the smaller complex exists in vivo or arises during lysis is unresolved. Cog1/2 knockout experiments and new Cog1/7 microscopy are not COG5 experiments. Selected original Results/Discussion and legends were read, not every figure.

Normal abstract retained. Original full text at https://www.researchgate.net/publication/13493088_Purification_and_Characterization_of_a_Novel_13_S_Hetero-oligomeric_Protein_Complex_That_Stimulates_in_VitroGolgi_Transport was read in the Golgi transport methods, antibody-inhibition Results and Figure 10 legend/localization text. Functional material is bovine, donor/acceptor Golgi are CHO, and NRK-52E cells provide microscopy. IgG inhibition with noninhibitory Fab is not isolated COG5 depletion/reconstitution. Notes provide checkable locators and a short control excerpt.

Protected abstract retained. The original author-uploaded article was read at https://www.researchgate.net/publication/8652574_The_Binary_Interacting_Network_of_the_Conserved_Oligomeric_Golgi_Tethering_Complex. Experimental Procedures/Table I identify human constructs and rabbit reticulocyte lysate. Results on binary interactions and COG6/COG8 incorporation establish cooperative assembly; purified binary affinities remain unproven. The notes give exact section locators and one short methods excerpt.

Selected full source Methods/Results/Discussion and legends were read. COG5-specific stability and ultrastructure findings are distinguished from assays performed on representative COG knockout subsets.

Selected exact-main cache contains an abstract and Introduction/Discussion, not complete Methods/Results. Those passages and all four exact BioPlex target/paper/partner records were read. Record-specific bait/prey/host metadata are retained.

Complete available abstract read; no full Methods claim. It reports the COG5 splice defect, impaired BFA-induced Golgi-to-ER redistribution and wild-type cDNA rescue. This is supporting human retrograde-trafficking evidence linked to the existing transport assessment, not a direct intra-Golgi flux measurement.

Selected full Methods/Results were read, including BFA assay Methods and Figure 6 Results. Patient fibroblasts expressing GalT-GFP show delayed Golgi-to-ER redistribution. The introduction explains BFA-induced tubular Golgi collapse; this paper does not newly perform the cDNA rescue reported in PMID:19690088. These results corroborate trafficking dysfunction without resolving a separate COG5 vesicle-mediated Golgi-to-ER step.
Actual selected full human construct/cell Methods and Golgi/stress Results were read. Human constructs, mouse N1E-115 cells, HEK293 cells and PERK-driven mouse retinal experiments are distinguished.

Actual selected full co-immunoprecipitation/rescue/copper Methods, Results and Discussion were read. Patient EBV-transformed lymphocytes and HEK293T loss/rescue models are distinguished. The source acknowledges model limits and conflicting clinical variant evidence; it is not used to assign copper-transporter or respiratory catalysis to COG5.

ontology.label: membrane
ontology.definition: A lipid bilayer along with all the proteins and protein complexes embedded in it and attached to it.

ontology.label: protein-macromolecule adaptor activity
ontology.definition: An adaptor activity that brings together two or more macromolecules in contact, permitting those molecules to function in a coordinated way. The adaptor can bring together two proteins, or a protein and another macromolecule such as a lipid or a nucleic acid.

ontology.label: enzyme binding
ontology.definition: Binding to an enzyme, a protein with catalytic activity.

ontology.label: Golgi apparatus
ontology.definition: A membrane-bound cytoplasmic organelle of the endomembrane system that further processes the core oligosaccharides (e.g. N-glycans) added to proteins in the endoplasmic reticulum and packages them into membrane-bound vesicles. The Golgi apparatus operates at the intersection of the secretory, lysosomal, and endocytic pathways.

ontology.label: cytosol
ontology.definition: The part of the cytoplasm that does not contain organelles but which does contain other particulate matter, such as protein complexes.

ontology.label: COG complex
ontology.definition: A multisubunit tethering complex of the CATCHR family (complexes associated with tethering containing helical rods) that has a role in tethering vesicles to the Golgi prior to fusion. Composed of 8 subunits COG1-8.

ontology.label: protein domain specific binding
ontology.definition: Binding to a specific domain of a protein.

ontology.label: helical-bundle zippering fusogenic activity
ontology.definition: Acting as a marker to identify a membrane and interacting selectively with one or more SNAREs on another membrane to mediate membrane fusion.

ontology.label: intra-Golgi vesicle-mediated transport
ontology.definition: The directed movement of substances within the Golgi, mediated by small transport vesicles. These either fuse with the cis-Golgi or with each other to form the membrane stacks known as the cis-Golgi reticulum (network).

ontology.label: Golgi membrane
ontology.definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding any of the compartments of the Golgi apparatus.

ontology.label: inter-Golgi cisterna vesicle-mediated transport
ontology.definition: The directed movement of substances from one Golgi cisterna to another, mediated by small transport vesicles.

ontology.label: retrograde transport, vesicle recycling within Golgi
ontology.definition: The retrograde movement of substances within the Golgi, mediated by COP I vesicles. Cis-Golgi vesicles are constantly moving forward through the Golgi stack by cisternal progression, eventually becoming trans-Golgi vesicles. They then selectively transport membrane and luminal proteins from the trans- to the medial-Golgi while leaving others behind in the trans-Golgi cisternae; similarly, they selectively move proteins from the medial- to the cis-Golgi.

ontology.label: Golgi organization
ontology.definition: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of the Golgi apparatus.

ontology.label: protein complex scaffold activity
ontology.definition: A structural molecule activity of a protein-containing complex component that serves to hold the complex together. Protein complex scaffolds are integral members of complexes.

ontology.label: trans-Golgi network membrane
ontology.definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding any of the compartments that make up the trans-Golgi network.
